Quick Gold Rate Facts

  • 24K: highest-purity gold listed on this page.
  • 22K: commonly referenced for jewellery pricing.
  • 21K / 20K / 18K: lower-purity categories with proportionally lower bullion value per weight.
  • Tola: a commonly used unit in Pakistan's gold market.
  • 10 grams: a useful standard weight for comparing quoted rates.
  • International rate: the source page lists 24K gold at $4,160 per ounce for this snapshot.

Understanding the Market

What Affects the Gold Rate in Sargodha?

The gold rate seen in Sargodha does not move independently from the wider bullion market. International gold prices, exchange-rate movements, local supply and demand, and revisions in the local jewellery market can all affect the quoted rate. That is why a rate shown earlier in the day may not remain unchanged later.

For buyers: compare the purity, net gold weight and written making charges instead of comparing only the headline per-tola number. The final price of a ring, necklace, bangle or bridal set can be different from the raw bullion benchmark.

24K vs 22K vs 21K vs 20K vs 18K

Karat indicates the proportion of pure gold in an alloy. A higher karat means a higher proportion of gold, while lower-karat jewellery contains more alloying metals. The daily value therefore changes with both purity and weight.

  • 24K: 24 parts out of 24 are represented as pure gold.
  • 22K: 22 parts out of 24 are gold.
  • 21K: 21 parts out of 24 are gold.
  • 20K: 20 parts out of 24 are gold.
  • 18K: 18 parts out of 24 are gold.

Gold Rate Per Tola, Per 10 Gram and Per Gram

Pakistani gold-market quotes are commonly discussed per tola, while international and retail comparisons may use grams or 10 grams. A standard tola is about 11.664 grams. When converting a quoted tola price into an approximate per-gram benchmark, divide the tola value by 11.664; for an internal check against this source page, the calculator below uses its 10-gram table.

Is the Gold Rate the Same as the Jewellery Price?

No. A jewellery quotation can include the actual gold weight, the selected purity, making or labour charges, stone or bead work and other applicable costs. For an accurate purchase calculation, ask the jeweller for a written breakdown of the metal rate, net weight and additional charges.
